$note: Shared reviewers.yml parser corpus. Driven from BOTH hand-ported implementations of the
same schema so their parity is executable rather than asserted by a comment:
refresh-reviewers WRITES the file assign-reviewers READS, so a divergence means the drift
generator rewrites lists the runtime reads differently. Add a case here, never to one suite.
Contract: `configs[].text` is the literal document (newlines already embedded; the CRLF case
carries \r\n). `configs[].expected` is the parsed config — the Python side returns
(config, locations) and only the config half is compared here, because `locations` has no JS
counterpart and stays covered by test_generate.py's own rewrite tests.
`globs[].cases[]` are path/verdict pairs for the glob->RegExp translator.
Characters that would be invisible or ambiguous in this file (U+FEFF, U+0085, U+001C, U+00A0)
are written as JSON \u escapes on purpose — keep them escaped rather than pasting the literal.
Both path filters (test-assign-reviewers.yml, test-refresh-reviewers.yml) watch this file, so
editing it runs both suites — a corpus tweak that only satisfies one port cannot land green.

configs.name: flow sequences
configs.why: the shape refresh-reviewers emits by default
configs.text:
default_pool: [generalist, alice]
rules:
  - paths: ["src/api/**"]
    reviewers: [alice, bob]
  - paths: ["src/ui/**"]
    reviewers: [carol]

configs.name: block sequences
configs.why: hand-written configs indent their lists instead
configs.text:
default_pool:
  - generalist
  - alice
rules:
  - paths:
      - "**/api/**"
      - docs/*.md
    reviewers:
      - bob

configs.name: comment stripping respects quotes
configs.why: a '#' inside a quoted scalar is data; one after whitespace starts a comment
configs.text:
# routing for the example repo
default_pool: ['alice', "bob"]  # trailing comment
rules:
  # which paths alice owns
  - paths: ["src/#hash/**"]   # the # above is data
    reviewers: ["ca#rol", 'dave']

configs.name: unterminated quote swallows the comment marker
configs.why: the in-quote state machine never re-closes, so nothing on the line is stripped

configs.name: multi-line flow sequence stops at the opening line
configs.why: no `]` on the line, so both ports fall back to s[1:] and the outer loop drops the continuation as an unrecognized indented key — they agree, and the corpus pins that they keep agreeing

configs.name: one-character quote is not a quoted empty string
configs.why: without the length>=2 guard a lone quote unquotes to '' — the divergence this corpus pins

configs.name: CRLF line endings
configs.why: the JS splits on /\r?\n/ and the Python on a bare \n; both must still agree
configs.text:
default_pool: [generalist, alice]
rules:
  - paths: ["src/api/**"]
    reviewers: [alice, bob]

configs.name: bare scalar values
configs.why: a scalar reviewers/paths value becomes a one-item list; a scalar default_pool does not
configs.text:
default_pool: generalist
rules:
  - paths: src/**
    reviewers: alice

configs.name: empty flow sequences and blank lines
configs.why: an empty [] is a parsed empty list, not an unparsed scalar

configs.name: indented decoys and unknown top-level keys are ignored
configs.why: only column-0 default_pool:/rules: open a section
configs.text:
version: 1
notes:
  default_pool: [mallory]
default_pool: [alice]
rules:
  - paths: ["a/**"]
    reviewers: [bob]

configs.name: rules terminated by a later top-level key
configs.why: section order is free; a column-0 key closes the rules block

configs.name: duplicate default_pool, flow then block
configs.why: YAML requires unique keys and both ports take PyYAML's de-facto last-wins, so the block form must REPLACE the flow list instead of appending to it

configs.name: duplicate default_pool, block then flow
configs.why: last-wins in the other order; the flow arm always replaced, and this pins that it keeps doing so

configs.name: duplicate default_pool, second one empty
configs.why: last-wins means an empty second key EMPTIES the pool, and the `rules:` after it still parses

configs.name: leading BOM before the first key
configs.why: a leading U+FEFF is legal YAML; JS trim() tolerated it and Python strip() did not, so the BOM is now stripped from the document on both sides

configs.name: leading BOM before a comment line
configs.why: the BOM strip and the space-or-tab comment rule must agree on the commonest BOM document of all, one that opens with a header comment

configs.name: U+0085 before # is not a comment
configs.why: NEL is isspace() in Python but not /\s/ in JS, so the ports disagreed until both required a space or a tab

configs.name: U+FEFF before # is not a comment
configs.why: the mirror image: U+FEFF is /\s/ in JS but not isspace() in Python; only a MID-document BOM reaches this test, the leading one is stripped first

configs.name: U+001C before # is not a comment
configs.why: FILE SEPARATOR is isspace() in Python but not /\s/ in JS, the same disagreement as U+0085 from a different character class

configs.name: tab before # starts a comment
configs.why: s-white is space OR tab, so narrowing the rule must not drop the tab half

configs.name: space before # starts a comment
configs.why: the other half of s-white, pinned beside the tab so neither can be narrowed away

configs.name: U+FEFF at the start of a flow token is kept
configs.why: JS trim() strips U+FEFF and Python strip() does not, so this token used to arrive with the BOM on one port and without it on the other; s-white trims neither

configs.name: U+0085 at the end of a flow token is kept
configs.why: the mirror image: Python strip() strips NEL and JS trim() does not; s-white trims neither

configs.name: U+001C at the end of a flow token is kept
configs.why: Python strip() strips FILE SEPARATOR and JS trim() does not, the same disagreement as U+0085 from a different character class

configs.name: U+00A0 padding around a flow token is kept
configs.why: the one character both ports agreed on and both got wrong — strip() and trim() BOTH drop NBSP, so a login padded with it used to look routable; s-white keeps it literal, so the runtime and the drift generator now agree it does not route

configs.name: U+FEFF at the start of a block item is kept
configs.why: the block arm trims separately from the flow arm, so the JS-strips-BOM divergence has to be pinned on both; only a MID-document BOM reaches here, the leading one is stripped first

configs.name: U+0085 at the end of a block item is kept
configs.why: Python strip() used to drop the trailing NEL from a block item while JS trim() kept it

configs.name: U+FEFF inside a rule's flow reviewers is kept
configs.why: a rule's reviewers list trims through its own path (setKey / set_key, then unquote), so the JS-strips-BOM divergence is pinned there too

configs.name: U+001C at the end of a block reviewer is kept
configs.why: the last trim path left: a block reviewer under a rule, where Python strip() used to drop the trailing FILE SEPARATOR and JS trim() kept it

configs.name: two leading BOMs: only one is stripped
configs.why: the explicit single-BOM strip is now the ONLY thing removing a BOM on either port; JS trim() used to absorb the second one and parse the key, Python strip() never did

configs.name: U+0085 before a top-level key is not indentation
configs.why: Python strip() used to remove the leading NEL so the line still matched `default_pool:`, while JS trim() left it and skipped the line; s-white leaves it on both, and indentOf/_indent_of count spaces only, so the line is column 0 either way

configs.name: tab padding around a flow token is trimmed
configs.why: narrowing the trim to s-white must not drop the tab half of it — this is the case that reds if either port is retuned to trim spaces only

configs.name: a bare CR ending the last line is data, not a line break
configs.why: a CR is a line break only when a newline FOLLOWS it — JS splits on /\r?\n/ and keeps this one, and the Python port must split the same way rather than stripping a trailing CR off each piece of a split("\n"), which would eat it. The runtime is the reference: the drift generator has to model what routes, and neither side trims CR as s-white any more

globs.why: trailing ** crosses segments but still requires the parent directory
leading **/ is optional leading directories, not a required one
**/ collapses to nothing at depth zero
a ** not followed by / is a bare .* and still crosses separators
a single * stays inside one segment
the common docs rule — optional dirs plus an in-segment star
regex metacharacters in a glob are literals
brackets are escaped, never a character class
